title: Caffeine vs Pre-Workout
meta_desc: Compare caffeine and pre-workout supplements for your NZ gym routine. Learn about coffee as a pre-workout, caffeine dose, and affordable options.
intro: As a gym-goer in New Zealand, you're likely looking for ways to boost your workout performance. Two popular options are caffeine and pre-workout supplements. But which one is better? In this guide, we'll explore the benefits of coffee as a pre-workout, the ideal caffeine dose, and compare cheap caffeine to expensive pre-workouts. We'll also discuss how to avoid the crash that can come with caffeine consumption.

sections.heading: Coffee as a Pre-Workout
sections.body: Coffee is a natural source of caffeine that can be used as a pre-workout. The caffeine in coffee can help increase alertness, boost energy, and enhance endurance. In New Zealand, you can find coffee at most supermarkets, such as Countdown or New World, for around $5-$10 per packet. A standard cup of coffee typically contains around 95mg of caffeine.
list: 1-2 cups of coffee 30 minutes before a workout
Black coffee or with a small amount of milk and sugar to avoid added calories

sections.heading: Caffeine Dose for Performance
sections.body: The ideal caffeine dose for performance varies from person to person, but research suggests that 1.5-3mg of caffeine per kilogram of body weight is effective. For a 70kg person, this would be around 105-210mg of caffeine. It's also important to note that individual tolerance and sensitivity to caffeine can vary greatly.
list: Start with a low dose and gradually increase as needed
Be mindful of other sources of caffeine, such as energy drinks or chocolate

sections.heading: Comparing Cheap Caffeine to Expensive Pre-Workouts
sections.body: Pre-workout supplements can be expensive, with some products costing upwards of $50-$100 per container. In contrast, a packet of coffee or a bottle of caffeine tablets can be purchased for under $20. However, it's essential to consider the other ingredients and benefits that pre-workout supplements may offer, such as protein, creatine, or branched-chain amino acids (BCAAs).

sections.heading: Avoiding the Crash
sections.body: To avoid the crash that can come with caffeine consumption, it's crucial to stay hydrated and eat a balanced meal or snack after your workout. You can also consider adding a source of protein, such as a protein shake or a handful of nuts, to help stabilize your energy levels. Exercise NZ's subsidised gym scheme can also help you save money on gym memberships and supplements.
list: Drink plenty of water throughout the day
Eat a meal or snack with a balance of carbohydrates and protein within 30-60 minutes after your workout

sections.heading: Conclusion and Next Steps
sections.body: In conclusion, coffee can be a cost-effective and natural pre-workout option for New Zealand gym-goers. By understanding the ideal caffeine dose and comparing cheap caffeine to expensive pre-workouts, you can make an informed decision about what works best for you. Consider combining caffeine with affordable NZ protein sources, such as whey protein or eggs, to support your fitness goals.
